title: Tame Data Skew: Salting, Range Partitioning & Pruning
summary: Find hot partitions the way Spark's adaptive execution does, fix a hot-key aggregation with salting and an exact two-phase aggregate, salt a skewed join by replicating the small side, balance range partitions with sampled quantiles, and prune Hive-style partition directories.

hints.test_skew_ratio_known_values: Use statistics.median. All-zero sizes give 1.0. A zero median with a non-empty max gives float('inf'). Raise ValueError for an empty list.
hints.test_detect_skew_needs_factor_and_min_si: A partition is skewed only if size > factor * median AND size > min_size. Both comparisons are strict.
hints.test_two_phase_sum_is_exact: Phase 1 sums per (key, salt). Phase 2 must ADD the partial sums of a key together. Overwriting with the last partial keeps only one salt's share.
hints.test_salting_spreads_the_hot_key: Number rows across all partitions in order (i = 0, 1, 2, ...), give row i the salt i % num_salts, and shuffle by partition_for((key, salt), num_partitions). phase1_sizes counts the rows each partition receives.
hints.test_phase_two_receives_at_most_num_salt: After phase 1, each partition holds one partial sum per distinct (key, salt). Only those partials are shuffled again, by partition_for(key, num_partitions).
hints.test_salted_join_matches_plain_join: A left row of hot key k with salt s only meets right rows tagged (k, s). Copy each hot right row once per salt 0..num_salts-1, or most matches disappear. None keys never match.
hints.test_salted_join_replicates_small_side_a: Left: hot keys get salts 0, 1, 2, ... in a per-key round-robin and other keys get salt 0. Right: hot rows go to every salt, others to salt 0. replicated_rows counts the extra copies.
hints.test_range_boundaries_balance_skewed_dat: Sort the sample and take s[i * len(s) // n] for i = 1..n-1. Drop a split point that isn't strictly greater than the previous one. range_partition is bisect_right(bounds, value).
hints.test_hive_partition_paths_and_pruning: Paths look like col=value joined by '/'. None is written as __HIVE_DEFAULT_PARTITION__ and parsed back to None. A predicate on a column the path doesn't have can't prune that path.
hints.test_inputs_not_mutated: Use sorted() rather than list.sort(), and build new lists for every shuffle.
